jurisdiction.name: United Republic of Tanzania
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Tanzania has no AI law or bill. It steers AI through the Personal Data Protection Act 2022 and its 2023 regulations, which set rules on automated decisions, the Bank of Tanzania's 2024 fintech sandbox regulations, which expressly cover AI and machine-learning applications, the health ministry's 2022 AI policy framework, the education ministry's 2025 national guidelines on AI in education, and the ICT ministry's draft national AI strategy framework and AI ethics guidelines. A new e-Government standard on AI for public institutions was listed in 2026 but its text has not been published.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering Parliament's full bills list, the ICT ministry, the e-Government Authority, each line ministry and each sector regulator. The education guidelines were read from the ministry's own document server. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the defence, home affairs, agriculture, foreign affairs and public service ministries, the universities commission and the judiciary's library. The e-Government AI standard, digital education guidelines and strategy, and a reported public-service directive on AI misuse are tracked as leads.

The file name indicates a commented revision of 31 July 2025. No adopted final version was found on the Ministry's site as of October 2026.
instruments.summary: Draft national AI strategy framework from the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, aligned with Tanzania Development Vision 2050 and the Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034. It sets a vision, guiding principles and eight pillars (AI infrastructure; AI governance; skills and talent; innovation, research and entrepreneurship; inclusion and accessibility; data governance; partnership and collaboration; AI-powered transformation of production and service sectors). It proposes a Tanzania AI Observatory with a governance structure, an AI risk-management process and a monitoring, evaluation, learning and adaptation (MELA) framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Tanzania's first national AI strategy (draft); anchors the planned AI governance arrangements and the companion AI guidelines.

instruments.summary: Draft national guidelines from the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology for public and private stakeholders that develop, deploy or adopt AI. They set eight AI principles (valid and reliable, safe, managed bias, resilient, transparency, accountability, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced) and ten ethical-practice steps for entities (code of ethics, diverse training data, monitoring, ethical reviews, staff education, risk anticipation). They add expectations on transparency, explainability, human oversight and telling users when they are interacting with an AI system.

instruments.official_title: Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Tanzania Health Sector
instruments.english_title: Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Tanzania Health Sector
instruments.current_status: Published by the Ministry of Health (cover dated February 2022); cited in the 2025 draft National AI Strategy Framework as an existing sector instrument. No later revision found.
instruments.summary: Ministry of Health framework setting out the processes, technologies, capabilities, stakeholders, principles and recommendations to guide the implementation and use of AI in the health sector, building on the existing digital health and data landscape. It reviews AI pilots and the role of the Centre for Digital Health, and lists what is needed: a shared vision, an enabling policy environment, leadership and coordination, quality assurance and oversight, ethical safeguards, capacity building and a review of related rules such as TMDA medical-device policies. It is meant to be the basis for future national health AI policies and regulatory mechanisms.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First sectoral AI governance document in Tanzania (health).

instruments.official_title: Sheria ya Ulinzi wa Taarifa Binafsi, 2022
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 11 of 2022, Cap. 44)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of the United Republic of Tanzania
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 May 2023 (GN No. 326 of 2023). Enacted in Swahili (Act No. 11 of 2022, Act Supplement of 2 December 2022); an official English version was published by the Attorney General as GN No. 395B of 13 June 2023 (Chapter 44) and is on the PDPC website. Applies to Mainland Tanzania and to union matters in Zanzibar. Passed by Parliament on 1 November 2022 (as stated at the end of the Act).
instruments.summary: Tanzania's data protection law, which sets principles for collecting and processing personal data, requires registration of data controllers and processors, and establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission. Section 36 lets a data subject require that decisions significantly affecting them are not based solely on automated processing; where they are, the controller must notify the data subject, who may ask for reconsideration (exceptions for contracts, written law or explicit consent). Section 33 gives a right to be told the logic of solely automated decisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main binding rule on automated decision-making and AI training/use of personal data.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Swahili Act Supplement No. 11 (Gazette No. 45 Vol. 103, 2 December 2022) read via pdftotext from the MICIT acts page; official English version (GN No. 395B of 13 June 2023, Chapter 44) read from https://pdpc.go.tz/documents/3/PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_ACT_2022.pdf, which gives the commencement date 1 May 2023 (GN No. 326 of 2023)

instruments.official_title: The Personal Data Protection (Personal Data Collection and Processing) Regulations, 2023
instruments.english_title: The Personal Data Protection (Personal Data Collection and Processing) Regulations, 2023
instruments.issuing_authority: Minister responsible for communication (Ministry of Communication and Information Technology)
instruments.current_status: Official English version published as GN No. 449C on 4 July 2023 under section 84(4) of the Interpretation of Laws Act; the Swahili original was not located online. Made by the Minister responsible for communication under section 64 of the Act (regulation 2 definition); effective date not stated in the version read.
instruments.summary: Regulations under the Personal Data Protection Act setting procedures for collecting and processing personal data. Regulation 19 requires controllers and processors to notify data subjects in writing when a decision significantly affecting them is based solely on automated processing, and gives a right to reject such use. Regulation 33 requires a data protection impact assessment before automated decision-making with significant legal effect that uses profiling or algorithmic means, and the privacy-by-design rules call for human intervention to minimise biases created by automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding algorithmic-decision notice and impact-assessment duties.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): official English version (GN No. 449C published 4 July 2023, made under section 64 of the Act) read via pdftotext from the PDPC publications page https://pdpc.go.tz/publications/

instruments.official_title: National Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence in Education
instruments.english_title: National Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence in Education
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
instruments.current_status: Published by the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (cover dated January 2025) on its guidelines page. The Ministry's 2025 national digital education guidelines for schools/teacher colleges and for TVET refer back to these guidelines in their AI sections.
instruments.summary: National guidelines from the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology on the ethical and responsible adoption, use and development of AI across primary, secondary, teacher, vocational and university education, aligned with the National Digital Education Strategy 2024/25-2029/30. They set out ten dimensions (policy and advocacy; security, privacy and ethics; teaching and learning; assessment; capacity building; curriculum; AI infrastructure; data use; research; partnerships) with actions that all education and training stakeholders 'shall' take, including adopting institutional AI policies, complying with data privacy laws, auditing AI tools for bias and keeping AI assessment tools fair and transparent. They also assign roles to the ministries, regulators (such as TCU and NACTVET) and institutions, and set a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national AI-specific guidance for the education sector; requires every institution to adopt its own AI-use framework.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): the Ministry website's document endpoint (www.moe.go.tz/endpoint?path=publications) lists 'NATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EDUCATION' with this file; full 40-page PDF (17 MB) read via pdftotext; cover and title page 'January, 2025', 'Published by: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology', foreword signed by Permanent Secretary Prof. Carolyne I. instruments.official_title: The Bank of Tanzania (Fintech Regulatory Sandbox) Regulations, 2024
instruments.english_title: The Bank of Tanzania (Fintech Regulatory Sandbox) Regulations, 2024
instruments.current_status: Published as GN No. 540 on 5 July 2024 (Gazette No. 25 Vol. 105). The regulations do not state a commencement date, so no effective date is recorded. The Bank's circulars page lists an official announcement inviting applications to the sandbox dated 20 December 2024.
instruments.summary: Regulations under the Bank of Tanzania Act setting up the Bank's Fintech Regulatory Sandbox, in which licensed financial service providers and fintech companies test innovative financial solutions not covered by existing law under the Bank's supervision. The definition of 'financial solution' expressly includes artificial intelligence and machine learning applications, alongside big data analytics and distributed ledger technology. Participants are evaluated within 45 days, test for up to twelve months (extendable), and must keep records of issues observed, risk mitigation and customer participation, report progress and protect customer data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding regulatory sandbox that explicitly covers AI and machine-learning financial solutions.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 17-page PDF read via pdftotext: GN No. 540 published on 5/7/2024, Supplement No. 26 to Gazette No. 25 Vol. 105 of 5 July 2024, made under section 70(1) of the Bank of Tanzania Act (Cap. 197), signed by the Minister for Finance at Dodoma on 24 June 2024. WebFetch of the Bank's regulations listing (publications/Filter/38) shows 'FINTECH REGULATORY SANDBOX REGULATIONS 2024' (24 Sep 2024) linking to this file.

changes.title: Draft Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of AI published
changes.detail: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology posts the draft guidelines on its guidelines page, dated 15-06-2025.

changes.title: Bank of Tanzania Fintech Regulatory Sandbox Regulations, 2024 published
changes.detail: GN No. 540 published 5 July 2024; sandbox open to financial solutions including AI and machine-learning applications.

changes.title: Personal Data Protection (Collection and Processing) Regulations, 2023 published
changes.detail: GN No. 449C published 4 July 2023; includes automated-decision notice (reg. 19) and DPIA (reg. 33) duties.

changes.title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 comes into force
changes.detail: Commencement on 1 May 2023 under GN No. 326 of 2023, as stated in the official English version.

changes.title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 published
changes.detail: Act No. 11 of 2022 published in the Act Supplement to Gazette No. 45 Vol. 103 of 2 December 2022.

leads.title: DTZS ISO/IEC 23894:2023 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Guidance on risk management (draft Tanzania Standard, EDC 4 (3131))
leads.english_title: Draft Tanzania Standard adopting ISO/IEC 23894:2023 on AI risk management
leads.note: Draft adoption for public comment indexed at https://www.tbs.go.tz/uploads/publications/en-1739785415-EDC 4 (3131) DTZS ISO_IEC 23894-2023 ... .pdf; the file now returns 404 (curl) / 503 (WebFetch). Check whether TBS has published the final TZS adoption (also check ISO/IEC 42001/22989).

leads.title: National AI legal framework (Attorney General's Office / MICIT)
leads.english_title: Planned AI law or ICT/emerging-technologies law
leads.issuing_authority: Office of the Attorney General; Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
leads.note: News reports (2024-2025) say the government is preparing an AI legal framework and an ICT law covering emerging technologies. No bill found on Parliament's site; pending.

leads.title: Mkakati wa Taifa wa Uchumi wa Kidijitali 2024 - 2034 (Tanzania Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
leads.note: Official PDF on mawasiliano.go.tz read: AI appears only as one emerging technology under Pillar 4 (Digital Innovation Culture and Enabling Technologies); no AI pillar, so kept as a lead under the scope test.

leads.title: Viwango na Miongozo ya Usimamizi, Utekelezaji na Matumizi yanayowajibika ya Akili Unde (AI) katika Taasisi za Umma (eGA/EXT/APA/011, Toleo 1.0, Agosti 2026)
leads.english_title: Standards and Guidelines for the Governance, Implementation and Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Public Institutions (eGA/EXT/APA/011, version 1.0, August 2026)
leads.note: Named in the e-Government Authority's official 'Orodha ya Viwango na Miongozo ya Serikali Mtandao' (list of current e-Government standards and guidelines, September 2026) at https://www.ega.go.tz/uploads/publications/sw-1791445249-Orodha%20ya%20Viwango%20na%20Miongozo%20ya%20Serikali%20Mtandao%20-%20Sept%20-%202026.pdf. The standard itself is not published on the eGA website (its documents pages list only the Act, regulations, policies and this list). Promote when the full text is reachable; likely public-sector, mandatory in scope for public institutions under the e-Government Act.

leads.title: National Digital Education Guidelines for Schools and Teacher Colleges; for Technical and Vocational Education and Training; for Universities (January 2025)
leads.english_title: National Digital Education Guidelines (schools and teacher colleges, TVET, universities), January 2025
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
leads.note: Official PDFs on cms.moe.go.tz read: the schools/teacher colleges and TVET guidelines each have a section 2.14 on the use of AI that refers back to the National Guidelines for AI in Education; the universities version mentions AI only briefly. General digital-education instruments, kept as leads under the scope test.

leads.title: National Digital Education Strategy, 2024/25 - 2029/30
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
leads.note: Official PDF on cms.moe.go.tz read (cover October 2024 / January 2025): AI appears among emerging technologies, not as a pillar; parent strategy of the AI in Education guidelines. Lead under the scope test.

leads.title: Public service directive on misuse of AI by public servants (June 2026)
leads.english_title: Public service directive on misuse of AI by public servants (June 2026)
leads.issuing_authority: President's Office, Public Service Management and Good Governance
leads.note: News reports (June 2026) say the minister directed disciplinary action against public servants who use AI in breach of public service ethics. No official circular found; utumishi.go.tz did not respond.

leads.title: Standards on use of AI in arbitration and alternative dispute resolution (reported July 2026)
leads.english_title: Standards on use of AI in arbitration and ADR (reported July 2026)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Constitutional and Legal Affairs (unconfirmed)
leads.note: Only one non-official tech-news site reports that standards on AI in arbitration were published on 26 July 2026. No official document, Government Notice or ministry page found; unverified.
